config.title: Build typed design tokens model

intro.title: Build typed design tokens model
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed design tokens model using TypeScript. Design tokens are reusable values like colors, spacing, and typography that define a design system. You will learn to use TypeScript's core concepts of interfaces and types to create a strongly-typed, self-documenting model for these tokens. This will involve defining structured types for different token categories and ensuring type safety across your design system. By the end, you'll have a foundational model that can be extended and integrated into larger projects.
intro.usecase: A typed design tokens model is foundational in large-scale design systems used by companies like Shopify or Airbnb. Developers use it to enforce consistent spacing, colors, and typography across product dashboards, marketing sites, and mobile apps. For example, a dashboard's card components, modal overlays, and form inputs all rely on these tokens to maintain visual harmony and simplify theme switching. This approach prevents style bugs and speeds up UI development when building or updating features.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface to define the structure of design tokens
Implement a typed object that represents a complete design tokens model
Apply union types to create variant options for design token values
Configure nested token structures using TypeScript type definitions
Initialize and manipulate typed design token objects with proper type safety
Integrate the typed design tokens model into a TypeScript project structure
Update token values while maintaining type constraints and validation

steps.title: Create the DesignTokens interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named DesignTokens to define the structure of design tokens.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and curly braces to define properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: An interface named DesignTokens is created with typed properties for design tokens.
successCriteria: The DesignTokens interface is defined with the correct name and structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the interface, but make sure it's named exactly 'DesignTokens' and uses the 'interface' keyword.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface wasn't created correctly. Remember to use 'interface DesignTokens' with curly braces to define the structure.

steps.title: Define the ColorTokens type
steps.instruction: Create a type named ColorTokens with properties for primary, secondary, background, text, and border colors. Each property should be a string representing a color value.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword followed by the type name and an object with string properties.
steps.seedCode:
// Create the DesignTokens interface here

// Define the ColorTokens type here
steps.expectedOutcome: A ColorTokens type with five string properties is defined.
successCriteria: The ColorTokens type exists with properties: primary, secondary, background, text, and border, all typed as strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your ColorTokens type includes all five properties: primary, secondary, background, text, and border, each typed as string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ColorTokens type is missing or incomplete. Create a type with properties for primary, secondary, background, text, and border colors, all as strings.

steps.title: Define the SpacingTokens type
steps.instruction: Define a type named SpacingTokens using a union of string literals for spacing values: 'xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'.
steps.hint: Use the `type` keyword followed by the type name and equals sign, then list the string literals separated by pipes (|).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: another union type for sizes
type SizeTokens = 'small' | 'medium' | 'large';
steps.expectedOutcome: A SpacingTokens type is created with the five specified string literal values.
successCriteria: The SpacingTokens type is defined with the union of 'xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a type, but it's missing some spacing values or has incorrect ones. Check that you included exactly 'xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The SpacingTokens type is not correctly defined. Make sure to use the `type` keyword and list all five string literals separated by pipes.

steps.title: Define the TypographyTokens type
steps.instruction: Define an interface named TypographyTokens with properties for fontFamily (string), fontSize (string), fontWeight (string), and lineHeight (string).
steps.hint: Create a new interface with the specified properties, each typed as string.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TypographyTokens interface with four string properties for typography design tokens.
successCriteria: The TypographyTokens interface is defined with fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight, and lineHeight properties, all typed as string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure all four properties (fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight, lineHeight) are included and typed as string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TypographyTokens interface is not correctly defined. Check that you have all four string properties.

steps.title: Define the BreakpointTokens type
steps.instruction: Define a new type named BreakpointTokens using a Record type that maps breakpoint names ('mobile', 'tablet', 'desktop') to number values.
steps.hint: Use the Record<Keys, Type> utility type to create a type where keys are strings and values are numbers.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Record type for sizes
type SizeTokens = Record<'small' | 'medium' | 'large', number>;
steps.expectedOutcome: A BreakpointTokens type is defined using Record<'mobile' | 'tablet' | 'desktop', number>.
successCriteria: The BreakpointTokens type is defined with Record and includes 'mobile', 'tablet', and 'desktop' keys mapped to number values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Check that you're using the Record utility type with the correct keys ('mobile', 'tablet', 'desktop') and number values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The BreakpointTokens type isn't defined correctly. Remember to use Record<'mobile' | 'tablet' | 'desktop', number>.

steps.title: Update the DesignTokens interface with the new types
steps.instruction: Update the DesignTokens interface to include properties for colors, spacing, typography, and breakpoints using the specific token types you defined earlier.
steps.hint: Add four properties to the DesignTokens interface: colors of type ColorTokens, spacing of type SpacingTokens, typography of type TypographyTokens, and breakpoints of type BreakpointTokens.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DesignTokens interface now has typed properties for colors, spacing, typography, and breakpoints, integrating all the specific token types.
successCriteria: The DesignTokens interface includes colors: ColorTokens, spacing: SpacingTokens, typography: TypographyTokens, and breakpoints: BreakpointTokens properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure all four properties (colors, spacing, typography, breakpoints) are included with their correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DesignTokens interface should have four properties using the types you defined earlier. Check that each property has the correct type annotation.

steps.title: Create a default tokens object
steps.instruction: Create a constant named defaultTokens of type DesignTokens with sample values for all properties. Use the types you've defined (ColorTokens, SpacingTokens, TypographyTokens, BreakpointTokens) to provide concrete values.
steps.hint: Declare a const variable with the type annotation : DesignTokens, then assign an object with properties matching the interface structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: A constant defaultTokens is declared with type DesignTokens and populated with sample values for colors, spacing, typography, and breakpoints.
successCriteria: defaultTokens is declared as a const variable with type DesignTokens, and contains valid values for all required properties (colors, spacing, typography, breakpoints).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure defaultTokens has all required properties (colors, spacing, typography, breakpoints) with values that match their respective types.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've declared defaultTokens as a const with type DesignTokens and provided values for all interface properties.

steps.title: Create a utility function to get a color token
steps.instruction: Define a function named getColor that accepts a keyof ColorTokens parameter and returns the corresponding color value from defaultTokens.
steps.hint: Create a function that takes a color key (like 'primary') and returns the color value from the tokens object.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed helper function that retrieves color values from the design tokens.
successCriteria: The getColor function is defined with a keyof ColorTokens parameter and returns the corresponding color value from defaultTokens.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function accepts a keyof ColorTokens parameter and returns the color value from the tokens object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. It should take a color key and return the matching color value from the tokens.

steps.title: Create a utility function to get a spacing token
steps.instruction: Define a function named getSpacing that accepts a SpacingTokens parameter and returns a CSS string with the spacing value (e.g., '1rem')
steps.hint: Create a function that takes a spacing token key and returns a string with the value and 'rem' unit.
steps.expectedOutcome: A getSpacing function is defined that takes a SpacingTokens parameter and returns a CSS string.
successCriteria: The getSpacing function is defined with the correct name, parameter type, and returns a string with 'rem' unit.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function accepts a SpacingTokens parameter and returns a string with 'rem' unit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check the name, parameter type, and return value.

steps.title: Export the types and utilities
steps.instruction: Export the DesignTokens interface, defaultTokens constant, and the getColor and getSpacing functions using export statements.
steps.hint: Add export before each declaration to make them available for import in other files.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DesignTokens interface, defaultTokens constant, getColor function, and getSpacing function are exported and ready to be used in other TypeScript files.
successCriteria: DesignTokens interface, defaultTokens constant, getColor function, and getSpacing function are exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've exported some items, but make sure to export all four: DesignTokens interface, defaultTokens constant, getColor function, and getSpacing function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The exports are missing or incorrect. Use export statements to make the DesignTokens interface, defaultTokens constant, getColor function, and getSpacing function available.
